questions.stem: How long may a navigation safety call last?
questions.explanation: Section 253(3) limits the call to one minute and to essential information.

questions.stem: In what order must the content of the call be given?
options: Intended action, identity, status, location, speed
Identity, location, intended action, present course and speed, status
questions.explanation: Section 253(3)(a) to (e) sets the sequence: identity, location, intended course of action, present course and speed, then status where applicable.

questions.stem: A vessel departs from a berth. When must the navigation safety call(s) be made?
options: 15 minutes before and again immediately before departure
Only when leaving a booming ground
questions.explanation: Section 253(2) requires two calls for departure.

questions.stem: Which of these is a circumstance requiring a call?
options: Nearing a bend where an approaching vessel cannot be seen
questions.explanation: Section 253(1)(e) lists nearing a bend or obstruction around which an approaching vessel cannot be seen.

questions.stem: A vessel in a narrow channel is about to overtake another. What does NSR 2020 require?
options: A call only after the overtaking
questions.explanation: Section 253(1)(c). The call does not replace the whistle signals.

questions.stem: Which of these is a status that the call may include?
questions.explanation: Section 253(3)(e) lists towing, not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, fishing other than trolling, constrained by draft, pilotage, at anchor and aground.

questions.stem: A towboat manoeuvres around a booming ground, will not impede others, and calls 15 minutes before its final departure. What does s. 253(4) say about the other two calls?
options: It must also call immediately before each manoeuvre
It need not make the dredge-approach or departure calls
questions.explanation: Section 253(4)(a) exempts such a towboat from the calls under (1)(i) and (j).

questions.stem: Two vessels agree by radio on a passing arrangement that breaks a steering and sailing rule. What governs?
options: The Collision Regulations still apply and whistle signals are still sounded
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 251: the radio rules do not relieve a vessel of its obligation to sound whistle signals or allow a breach of the steering and sailing rules.

questions.stem: In restricted visibility a vessel approaches a ferry route. Is a call required?
options: Yes, approaching a charted route (including a ferry route) in restricted visibility
Only for a vessel over 20 m
Only if a ferry is seen

questions.stem: Who makes the call if the person making it is not in charge of the deck watch?
options: No one needs to be told
Only the master is told at handover
They must repeat the call twice
They must tell the person in charge without delay

questions.stem: On which channel is the navigation safety call made by a vessel outside a BC traffic zone?
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 item 2(a) names Channel 16 outside a traffic zone; inside a zone it is the appropriate VHF channel.

questions.stem: You make a call but you are not the person in charge of the deck watch. What does s. 250(2) require?
options: You tell the person in charge of the deck watch without delay
You tell the master at handover
questions.explanation: Section 250(2). Also, a vessel in doubt about another vessel's actions or intentions must call (s. 253(1)(d)).
